contracts: AWS provider IDs must start with aws:///.
A placeholder instance name beginning with i-placeholder- must retain subsequent slashes.

findings.message: The placeholder alternative lacks a start anchor, so malformed IDs such as junkaws:///us-east-1a/i-placeholder-some pass validation. Previously both alternatives required aws:/// at the beginning, as required by the note's invalid-format boundary.
findings.evidence:
New regex: `^aws\:\/\/\/[-0-9a-z]*\/[-0-9a-z]*(\/[-0-9a-z\.]*)?$|aws\:\/\/\/[-0-9a-z]*\/%s.*$`
Previous placeholder alternative: `^aws\:\/\/\/[-0-9a-z]*\/(%s.*)$`
Validation rejects only when validAwsRefIdRegex.FindStringSubmatch(id) == nil.

findings.message: Placeholder names containing slashes are truncated. For aws:///us-east-1a/i-placeholder-some/arbitrary/cluster/local, Name becomes i-placeholder-some instead of the complete placeholder name, violating the note's preservation requirement.
findings.evidence:
splitted := strings.Split(id[7:], "/")
Name:       splitted[1],
Deleted test expected Name: "i-placeholder-some/arbitrary/cluster/local".
